A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Critique-Coder study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendix A are readable and support reliable matching across layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training and benchmark results, including coding evaluations, BBEH reasoning results, CRL-ratio ablations, and test-time scaling experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports the critique-data generator's pass@1 on the study's dataset in Section 2.2.

M1.justification: The hybrid GRPO procedure, 20% CRL mixture, candidate-solution generator, labeling threshold, reward functions, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Expanded training explanations introduce no new algorithmic component or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same rStar-Coder seed data, EvalPlus, BigCodeBench-Instruct, Aider-Polyglot, LiveCodeBench v5, and four BBEH subtasks. Sequential and parallel scaling scenarios are retained. The newly reported generator score uses existing dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains AceCoder-7B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-14B, DeepCoder-14B, DeepSeek-V2.5-238B, GPT-o1, and the same Qwen3 base/RL comparisons. Tables 4–5 also retain their comparison sets. The added generator-strength diagnostic does not introduce a comparator against CRITIQUE-CODER.

E3.justification: The stated filtering, training budgets, model sizes, sampling settings, checkpoint selection, ablation ratios, and scaling procedures remain unchanged. Newly explicit inference and optimization controls clarify existing experiments; no revised protocol is reported.

E4.justification: Section 2.2 adds a generator-strength diagnostic comparing its reported pass@1 with Qwen3-4B to support the argument against stronger-teacher distillation. Existing CRL-ratio ablations, generation analysis, and sequential/parallel scaling tests are retained without additional experimental variants.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed variation, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Sampling counts and existing descriptive statistics are unchanged; no uncertainty-reporting procedure is added.

E6.justification: Section 2.2 newly reports Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct pass@1 of 32.20%, compared with the retained Qwen3-4B value of 43.72%. Tables 1–5 and plotted results are unchanged. Section 3.5 newly describes further marginal scaling gains after four iterations, although Figure 5 shows a plateau.

T1.justification: The formal problem definitions, GRPO objective, and reward definitions in Equations 1–3 are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims: CRL complements standard RL, a 20% mixture improves coding performance, and benefits transfer to reasoning tasks. Expanded supporting discussion does not redefine the main contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3.7 narrows the self-critique limitation to final-answer-only evaluation and adds an explanation based on internalized judgment and unavailable reasoning trajectories. Section 2.2 argues against stronger-teacher distillation, while Section 3.6 explicitly frames judgment/solution mismatch as a hypothesis. These are interpretive refinements without new mechanism tests.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 newly identifies official publications or recommended settings as sources for external baseline results. Sections 3.4 and 3.6 explicitly state shared inference configurations and fixed ablation optimization settings. Existing hyperparameters, access information, and the Appendix A prompt remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and dedicated related-work section are unchanged. However, Section 3.7 newly connects the observed self-critique failure to already-cited Huang et al. and Valmeekam et al., while Section 2.2 explicitly distinguishes the setup from stronger-teacher distillation.

P1.justification: Substantial paragraph rewriting and expansion affects dataset/training explanations and most results discussions in Sections 3.3–3.7, especially transfer, scaling, ablations, and limitations. Section roadmaps are added and the publication header changes. This is extensive prose revision within the retained overall section structure.

P2.justification: The same five figures, six tables, and algorithm are retained. Algorithm 1 moves before the reward-function discussion; Figures 4–5 move to the following page, and Table 5 is separated from Table 4. These are limited placement and layout changes without new visualizations or redesigned tables.

improvement.justification: The added generator-strength measurement, clearer baseline provenance, and explicit ablation controls provide a modest improvement in evidence and transparency. The narrower self-critique limitation is also useful. These benefits are tempered by an untested causal explanation in Section 3.7 and the new claim of continued scaling gains despite Figure 5's plateau. The main method and benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
